Ager, E. and Sallstrom, M. (2023). High Temperature Heat Pumps in Paper Drying Processes: A Techno-Economic Analysis. Degree project in Energy Technology, second cycle, 30 credits, KTH Royal Institute of Technology, Stockholm. Title page year 2023 (the DiVA record and to-get.csv give 2024; the thesis cites 2024 sources and uses a Jan-Jun 2024 exchange rate). URL: https://kth.diva-portal.org/smash/get/diva2:1901790/FULLTEXT01.pdf

Locators are printed page numbers (PDF page = printed + 1; the table of contents is off by one from the printed footers in Ch. 5). A KTH MSc thesis on high-temperature heat pumps (HTHP) for paper drying with two Holmen case studies (Hallstavik and Braaviken integrated TMP mills, Sweden). Main file: Hallstavik PM11 and PM12 HTHPs on drying-hood exhaust (120 degC sink): capacity, average COP (as %), electricity per GJ heat derived from annual totals, unit and total capex per kW thermal, maintenance per kW and as 6% of unit cost, capacity factor, annual output; Braaviken 16 kW HTHP on TMP condensate (140 degC sink), same parameters; Hallstavik cylinder dryer steam 1.0-1.7 t/t paper (converted to MWh/t with the mill analogy 1.5 t steam = 1 MWh) and Holmen paper drying 4.4-5.6 GJ/t (Moya and Pavel 2018); Table 2 HTHP market overview (33 products, reprinted from Arpagaus et al. 2023): maximum heating capacity, maximum supply temperature, TRL and specific investment cost. The case-study COP and unit costs are not independent data: they come from the Arpagaus et al. (2023) correlations (Eq. 5, Eq. 14), and total CAPEX is unit cost x 3 by assumption. Flows: dryer steam mass per t paper. _measures.csv: the three HTHP retrofits (saving, CAPEX, payback). _other-values.csv: process temperatures, dryer-type shares, mill statistics, emission factors, correlations. Not loaded: figures (charts only), sensitivity analysis (Ch. 6, percent changes in payback), qualitative literature on cycles, compressors and refrigerants. Costs: no price year printed; 2023 used and flagged.
